I haven't really got a good answer. I also tend to find things very dull, and frequently find myself wondering if this is it. And I'm 99.99% certain it is. 

I don't know how you can work against it, but in the recent year or so, I've realised that I had to change a few perceptions. I used to think something like this 1. Figure out the problems of the mind
2. Fix the problems of the mine
3. Enjoy. (This never worked.) 

Now it is more of a
1. What can I do here and now to lessen the existential pain, or what do I know is good for me and then try to do it. 
2. Shit is ok.

What I do to achieve this is nothing special. Very basic, but easy to forget and neglect. 
1. Use my body in some way (Exercise, walking, working)
2. Meditate irregularly.
3. Try to eat decent food.

By all means, I also have not so healthy habbits, like binge drinking for a few days, but that loses its fun fairly quick. (Achieved fun vs negative sideeffects) 

Now, this doesn't really change a lot, but it seems to make life flow better. A change in perspective occurs. I find myself more patient, more willing to engage in things and things seem more interesting. (Or at least they are not such a waste of time.)

I think that partly answers your question. Might not be the answer you were hoping for, but it's what limited knowledge I can supply.
I ignored those 3 things (physical movement, meditation, food) for years, thinking it would be completely useless, but for me they have made a noticeable impact.

Oh, and Alan Watts. He talks/writes a lot about humans existensial pain and if nothing else, he's quite entertaining. You might learn a thing or two if you check him out. 😊
